title: KV cache shard reshuffle — postmortem and action synthesis
author: Lena Ortiz
content:
Summary:

This document is a consolidated postmortem and action synthesis for the KV-cache shard reshuffle that caused token-latency degradation and elevated 99th-percentile tail latencies for several multitenant workloads on 2023-11-27. It captures the timeline, contributing factors, measurements, immediate mitigations, and the long-term program of work (owners, deadlines, and dashboard/alert changes) required to avoid recurrence.

Impact (what happened):
- Start: 2023-11-27 09:17 UTC — observed elevated token-p90/p99 on the inference path for models served from the west-us region.
- Duration: ~3 hours of intermittent elevated tail latency with several short spikes to 1.2–1.8s token latency (baseline ~0.2–0.4s).
- Affected surface: ~12 production tenants (varied impact), control plane KV-cache rebalances triggered increased synchronous KV fetches and forced de-duplication across shards.
- Customer visible: A small subset of customers reported degraded chat responsiveness; automated health checks triggered incident page and paging for platform on-call.

Owner: Eng Platform — Operator Reliability (primary), Serving Runtime (secondary).
SLO impact: Estimated SLO burn at the platform layer: 0.9% SLO budget for tail latency across west-us models for the day. No SLA crediting was required but internal error budget thresholds were approached for a few tenants.

Timeline (verified events, logs, and operator notes):
1) 2023-11-27 09:12 UTC — automated preflight reported a degraded shard-imbalance metric (shard skew ratio > 1.6).
2) 09:15 — Autoscaler/maintenance agent scheduled a reshuffle job to reassign 48 KV shards across the west-us pool to improve cache hit distribution.
3) 09:17 — Platform telemetry: synchronous KV miss counts spiked by 6x; several worker processes entered contention while warming new hot shards.
4) 09:25 — On-call noticed increased inference tail latency; initiated immediate mitigation steps (see below).
5) 10:05 — Emergency rolling revert of the reshuffle started: held the shuffle progression and resumed only a small subset of shard moves.
6) 11:45 — Rebalance completed with stabilization; p99 returned to baseline by 12:15 UTC.

Measured diagnostics and supporting evidence:
- Metric snapshots (comparison to baseline week):
  - KV synchronous fetches: +540% at peak (09:18–09:30).
  - Cache hit rate (global, west-us): dropped from 92.3% -> 55.4% during reshuffle window.
  - Worker CPU queue length: median +30%, 95th +120%.
  - Tail token latency (per-token p99): baseline 0.37s -> peak 1.74s.
- Logs: operator-run logs show the maintenance agent issued parallel move operations without per-tenant slowdown throttles.
- Traces: distributed traces correlate KV-miss spike with sustained database RPS increase to backing stores (redis clusters) indicating higher synchronous fallback reads.

Root cause analysis (concise):
1) Primary cause — Aggressive parallel shard moves by the automated rebalance agent without respecting warmup backoff: the agent executed N concurrent shard copy operations (N=16) with no token-smoothing window, causing a coordinated reduction in local prefix/KV cache hit rate across many nodes.
2) Secondary cause — Lacking pre-move synthetic warmup: there was no pre-warm path to repopulate hot prefixes into the new shard locations before switching traffic. New nodes took traffic cold, incurring synchronous reads.
3) Contributing factor — Alerting and throttles were tuned for capacity deficits, not for coordinated cache rebalances; there was no soft-fail circuit to pause reshuffles when tail latency rose.
4) Operational process gap — Runbook guidance for shard rebalances did not require operator-approved staging or a canary batch size based on tenant heatmap.

Immediate mitigations performed (operator timeline):
- 09:25 UTC: Reduced concurrent move concurrency from 16 -> 2 via the maintenance agent override.
- 09:30 UTC: Enabled a temporary in-memory prefix fallback on a subset of hot-serving nodes to avoid synchronous reads to redis for top-5 tenants.
- 10:05 UTC: Rolled back uncommitted move batches and paused the reshuffle job; started phased resumption with canary batches (see runbook update below).

Action items and long-term fixes (owners, priority, target date):
1) Rewrite rebalance agent to support staged moves with pre-warm option (HIGH) — owner: eng-serving-runtime (Asha Patel), due: 2024-02-15.
2) Implement per-tenant heatmap and canary batch sizing (MEDIUM) — owner: eng-platform/operator-reliability (Miguel Tan), due: 2024-01-31.
3) Add a dynamic reshuffle circuit-breaker that pauses ongoing shard moves when tail latency or KV sync fetch rate exceeds thresholds (HIGH) — owner: eng-sre (Jordan Li), due: 2024-01-20.
4) Create synthetic pre-warm jobs that replay recent hot prefixes to target shards before traffic cutover (HIGH) — owner: eng-serving-runtime (Data Platform liaison), due: 2024-02-28.
5) Update runbooks and add a dedicated "Shard Movement Playbook" with checklist, operator approvals, and rollback commands (CRITICAL) — owner: eng-platform/runbooks (Lena Ortiz), due: 2024-01-08.
6) Dashboard and alerting improvements (see next section) (MEDIUM) — owner: telemetry-team (Rachel Huang), due: 2024-01-10.
7) Quarterly DR/gameday for cache reshuffle scenarios including synthetic load and cold-warm transitions (LOW) — owner: platform-ops (M. Tan), due: 2024-04-01.

Dashboard & alert changes (concrete proposals):
- New panel: "Shard Move Concurrency" (gauge) with alert if > 4 concurrent moves for > 2 minutes. Severity: P2.
- Alert: "KV sync-fetch surge" when rate increases > 3x baseline AND p99 token latency > 1s for 5m. Severity: P1 and auto-paginate on-call.
- SLO burnboard widget: per-tenant SLO contribution during rebalances (to quickly identify tenants approaching error budget).
- Add synthetic warmup success/failure metric (boolean per batch) to monitor pre-warm coverage.

Runbook updates (summary of changes to be merged):
- New section: "Performing a Shard Movement" with the following required steps:
  1) Review tenant heatmap and identify top-10 hot prefixes.
  2) Schedule maintenance window with operator sign-off if > 10% expected cold-hit exposure.
  3) Execute canary batch (<= 2 shards) with pre-warm enabled; validate cache-hit > 85% for top-3 tenants in 15m.
  4) Increase concurrency only after canary success and p99 latency within 10% of baseline for 30m.
  5) Rollback instructions and emergency throttle commands (copied CLI snippets below).
- Runbook authoring note: Must include the CLI snippet for throttle: `maintenance-agent set-concurrency --job-id $JOB --concurrency 2` and rollback: `maintenance-agent abort-moves --job-id $JOB --force`

Operational run commands (copyable):
- Pause reshuffle: `maintenance-agent pause --job-id <id>`
- Throttle concurrency: `maintenance-agent set-concurrency --job-id <id> --concurrency 2`
- Begin canary prewarm: `maintenance-agent prewarm --target-shard <shard-id> --lookback 60m`

Post-incident verification plan (tests & dashboards to validate fix):
- A/B test on next scheduled rebalance: run with new pre-warm enabled on 5% of shards and measure cache hit delta and tail latency for 60m.
- Run automated synthetic workload simulating top-50 prefixes against the pre-warm path; require > 85% cache hit on warmed shards.
- Add chaos experiments in platform lab that emulate staggered node failures plus reshuffles.

Follow-ups and owners (tracking table):
- Weekly check-ins for engineering owners until all high-priority items are closed. Meeting: "KV Rebalance Safety Sync" — cadence: weekly, owner: Lena Ortiz.
- Post-implementation audit due 2024-03-01: verify SLO behavior for a full month of scheduled reshuffles. Owner: eng-sre (Jordan Li).

Lessons learned (operational & cultural):
- Operational: Automated rebalancers must be conservative by default — favor small canary batches with explicit warmups over large parallel moves.
- Telemetry: The missing composite alert (KV sync-fetch + tail latency) delayed escalation. Combine metrics into correlated alerts where appropriate.
- Team practice: Runbooks must codify a human-in-the-loop checkpoint for any multi-node coordinated changes that affect cache locality.

Appendix A — Key logs and queries used during incident (examples):
- PromQL: `sum(rate(kv_sync_fetch_total[1m])) by (region)` — used to detect 6x surge.
- Tracing search: `trace.service=\"inference\" AND trace.tag.shard_move=true AND duration>1000` — used to identify requests impacted by cold shards.
- Redis RPS query: `avg_over_time(redis_commands_total[5m])` per instance to detect backing-store pressure.

Appendix B — Quick CLI snippets for operators (for runbook copy/paste):
- Pause/resume: `maintenance-agent pause --job-id 1234 && maintenance-agent resume --job-id 1234`
- Force rollback: `maintenance-agent abort-moves --job-id 1234 --force --notify-team ops`
- Canary run: `maintenance-agent run-canary --shard-list 12,13 --prewarm --verify-warm=15m`
